classification.difficultyReason: Translate a surface-area bound into a quadratic inequality, determine its sign interval and restrict the result to positive radii.

content.prompt: The surface area of a cylinder with fixed height $3\text{ cm}$ is given by $SA_{\mathrm{cyl}}=2\pi r(r+3)$. What values may $r$ take if $SA_{\mathrm{cyl}}$ is no greater than $8\pi\text{ cm}^2$?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\pi r(r+3)&\le8\pi\\r(r+3)&\le4\\r^2+3r-4&\le0\\(r+4)(r-1)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are $-4$ and $1$. Testing $r=-5,0,2$ gives products $6,-4,6$, respectively. The quadratic is non-positive between its zeroes, including the endpoints, so $-4\le r\le1$.

A cylinder has positive radius, so $0<r\le1\text{ cm}$.
